quote: looking at what that might be for if some companies will, you know, pay it, just they wanna have their company name out there so we could be like a rep or if it's payments throughout it.
stewart_read: Customer is asking whether Ion would sponsor or subsidize installation in exchange for brand placement/promotion — a sponsorship/partnership ask that has no defined answer in Ion's residential setter script. The rep does not address this at all before moving into verify.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this an unanswerable, closer-tier or even sales-leadership-tier question and correctly declined to engage rather than fabricate an answer — consistent with setter_scope_discipline's escape hatch.
coaching_implication: Manager should confirm whether Ion has any sponsorship/promotional program; if not, coach the rep to explicitly name that this isn't something Ion offers rather than letting it go unaddressed, since the customer may expect an answer and could be disappointed later.

quote: I, myself, am just the scheduler, so that's kind of the process of what we do.
stewart_read: This is actually the POSITIVE case of scope discipline — the rep declines to negotiate pricing/sponsorship terms and clearly names her role, deferring to the specialist. Flagged here as a model moment rather than a violation.
coaching_implication: Use this line as a positive example in coaching — clean, confident scope-holding language the manager can point other reps toward.

quote: Yeah. Exactly. So we'll need to we don't do the groundnuts here at ION, so we'll primarily focus on that Northern building.
stewart_read: Customer described a mixed-use, multi-structure nonprofit property considering a ground-mount layout — a scenario outside Ion's standard single-family residential script. The rep handles it inline by stating a company fact (no ground mounts) and redirecting to the roof, without pausing to flag internally that this property type itself may need special handling before booking. This is a plausible, well-supported reactive read, but the alternative — that stating a known company capability limit accurately IS the correct move and needs no escalation — is at least equally supported, since the rep had the fact readily available and used it correctly.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may simply have accurate, readily-available product knowledge (no ground mount) and applied it correctly in real time; no schema-defined non-standard-scenario protocol exists for this floor, so there is no rule being violated, only an unschematized gap in whether reps should flag mixed-use/nonprofit properties for supervisor review before booking.
coaching_implication: Ask the rep whether nonprofit/LLC-owned, multi-structure properties get flagged for any kind of pre-appointment review at Ion; if not, this is a process question for Kenny rather than a rep coaching gap on this call.

quote: Me being there within just a month and a half, it's about maybe 100 to 200.
stewart_read: Customer gives a bill range but qualifies it heavily (only lived there 6 weeks, mixed propane/wood-stove/electric usage). Rep logs it ("100 to 200. K.") and moves straight to the next verify item without reflecting the number back or using it to build curiosity about savings.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the property is nonprofit/educational and not a standard bill-pain-driven residential sale, the bill amount may carry less weight as a persuasion lever here, so the rep's flat capture-and-move-on could be an appropriate calibration to this atypical lead rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly acknowledge the number even on atypical leads — a short reflective line costs nothing and keeps the anchor-and-flip habit consistent across all call types.

quote: Do you know the name of the person?
stewart_read: Customer asks who the specialist will be; rep admits she doesn't know yet and explains the round-robin system transparently rather than fabricating a name.
coaching_implication: Positive knowledge-gap handling — honest, specific, no fabrication. Worth naming in the 1-on-1 as the right way to handle an unknown.

quote: K. No worries. Well, I'll go ahead. We'll we'll get started on some options here for you, and we'll give you a call Tuesday, 9AM.
stewart_read: Rep restates the day/time and the no-driving/email-access condition but never runs the explicit "is that fair?" handshake or confirms the one-hour block language from button_up. The close is functional but skips the verbal-commitment mechanic the schema flags as predictive of show rate.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep does include the no-driving/email-access condition ("make sure you're not driving... have access to your email"), which is most of button_up's substance, so this could be read as a near-complete close rather than a full miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close every booking with the explicit "is that fair?" question and the one-hour-block framing — small addition, directly tied to schema's show-rate signal.
